findings.source_passage: it may be deemed almost superfluous to establish the fact, that among people at large, the business of whaling is not accounted on a level with what are called the liberal professions
findings.why_it_matters: The ironic, mock-legalistic framing of the chapter's opening argument—the visiting-card gambit with 'S.W.F.' initials—establishes Ishmael's satirical register and is a distinctive voice-defining passage that sets up the entire advocacy conceit.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least the S.W.F. / visiting-card joke; it is the chapter's first ironic flourish and anchors the 'advocate' persona.

findings.source_passage: if a stranger were introduced into any miscellaneous metropolitan society…if in emulation of the naval officers he should append the initials S.W.F. (Sperm Whale Fishery) to his visiting card, such a procedure would be deemed pre-eminently presuming and ridiculous
findings.why_it_matters: The S.W.F. anecdote is a textually distinctive, satirically precise moment that critics regularly cite as an example of Ishmael's ironic social commentary; its erasure removes an interpretive keystone about class and professional status.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert a compressed version of the visiting-card anecdote before the butchery rebuttal to preserve the satirical architecture.

findings.source_passage: _The whale no famous author, and whaling no famous chronicler?_ Who wrote the first account of our Leviathan? Who but mighty Job! And who composed the first narrative of a whaling-voyage? Who, but no less a prince than Alfred the Great
findings.why_it_matters: The italicized call-and-response rhetoric—objection set up in normal type, refutation in italics—is a signature structural and prosodic device of this chapter; the draft collapses it into reported questions, erasing the performative courtroom voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the italicized restatement of each objection followed by the rhetorical question series; the typographic and rhetorical pattern is itself a signature of Ishmael's advocacy persona.

findings.source_passage: Good again; but then all confess that somehow whaling is not respectable. _Whaling not respectable?_ Whaling is imperial!
findings.why_it_matters: The escalating single-word italicized rebuttals ('_Whaling not respectable?_', '_No dignity in whaling?_') are a prosodic signature of the chapter's climax; the draft flattens them into quotation marks, softening the rhetorical punch.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the italicized restatement form (not quotation marks) for each objection-rebuttal pair to preserve the chapter's distinctive rhetorical escalation.

findings.source_passage: I know a man that, in his lifetime, has taken three hundred and fifty whales. I account that man more honorable than that great captain of antiquity who boasted of taking as many walled towns.
findings.source_locator: final paragraph before the 'as for me' coda
findings.why_it_matters: This concrete, name-less specimen of heroic whaleman—counterposed against the ancient general—is a rhetorically pointed flourish that bridges the constellation of Cetus to the personal 'as for me' peroration; its absence weakens the transition.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the one sentence about the man who took 350 whales before the Yale-and-Harvard closing paragraph.

summary: The draft preserves the famous closing sentence and the Egyptian-mother passage well, but erases the satirical S.W.F. visiting-card anecdote (the chapter's opening ironic keynote) and collapses the italicized call-and-response rebuttal structure that is the chapter's defining rhetorical signature, producing three medium-severity failures that together require regeneration.
